title: Concrete cone comparisons and their homotopy invariance
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be a small cochain dg category over $\mathbf Z$ as in [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure], with Hom differential $\partial$. Write $Z^0\mathcal A$ for closed degree-zero maps and $H^0\mathcal A$ for their classes modulo degree-minus-one boundaries. Assume (A) a zero object and dg binary sums, whose inclusions and projections are closed degree-zero maps satisfying the biproduct identities. Assume (B) dg functors $[n]$, $n\in\mathbf Z$, with $[0]=1$, $[n+m]=[n][m]$, and composition-compatible cochain isomorphisms $\mathcal A(x,y[n])\cong\mathcal A(x,y)[n]$, where $V[n]^j=V^{j+n}$ and $d_{V[n]}=(-1)^nd_V$. A sequence $u\xrightarrow{a}v\xrightarrow{b}w$ in $Z^0\mathcal A$ is called admissible when there are graded degree-zero maps $\pi:v\to u$ and $s:w\to v$ such that $\pi a=1$, $bs=1$, $a\pi+sb=1$, $ba=0$, and $\pi s=0$; its boundary is the closed map $\delta=\pi\partial s:w\to u[1]$ under (B). A map is an admissible monomorphism if it is the first arrow of such a sequence. Assume (C) that each closed degree-zero $f:x\to y$ has an admissible sequence $y\xrightarrow{i_f}c(f)\xrightarrow{p_f}x[1]$ with boundary $f[1]$. A homotopy equivalence is a closed degree-zero map with a closed degree-zero inverse modulo boundaries. (i) For an admissible sequence $x\xrightarrow{a}y\xrightarrow{b}z$ with splitting $(\pi,s)$ and boundary $\delta$, and a cone sequence $y\xrightarrow{i_a}c(a)\xrightarrow{p_a}x[1]$ with splitting $(\rho,\sigma)$, the maps $e=b\rho:c(a)\to z$ and $t=i_as-\sigma\delta:z\to c(a)$ are closed degree-zero maps satisfying $et=1_z$ and $te-1_{c(a)}=\partial H$ for some degree-minus-one $H$. Moreover $ei_a=b$ and $[-p_a]=[\delta e]$ in $H^0\mathcal A$. Thus $(1_x,1_y,[e])$ is an isomorphism of the associated diagrams. (ii) For closed degree-zero $f_k:x_k\to y_k$ ($k=1,2$), closed degree-zero $a:x_1\to x_2$, $b:y_1\to y_2$, and degree-minus-one $h$ satisfying $\partial h=bf_1-f_2a$, there is a closed degree-zero cone map $c:c(f_1)\to c(f_2)$ such that $[ci_{f_1}]=[i_{f_2}b]$ and $[p_{f_2}c]=[a[1]p_{f_1}]$ in $H^0\mathcal A$. If $a,b$ are homotopy equivalences, then so is $c$. These assertions apply to arbitrary chosen cones satisfying (C), without assuming a triangulated structure.
